exercises.prompt: Ask a fruit seller: “How much are the apples per jin?”
exercises.english: How much are the apples per jin?
exercises.explanation: 多少钱 asks the price. 一斤 at the end makes it a price per jin, a unit equal to 500 grams in mainland China.
块 is the everyday spoken unit for yuan. Give the price first and the unit of weight second.

exercises.prompt: Say: “It is a bit expensive.” Use the mild-complaint pattern.
exercises.explanation: 有点 before 贵 softens the complaint about the price.

exercises.prompt: Request: “Could it be a little cheaper?”
exercises.english: Could it be a little cheaper?
exercises.explanation: Put 一点 after 便宜 to ask for a small price reduction. 可以…吗 frames it as a request.

exercises.prompt: Say: “I would like two jin of apples.”
exercises.english: I would like two jin of apples.
exercises.explanation: Use 两 with the measure 斤, then name what you are buying, 苹果.

exercises.prompt: Say: “These apples are both big and sweet.”
exercises.pinyin: Zhèxiē píngguǒ yòu dà yòu tián.
exercises.english: These apples are big and sweet.
exercises.explanation: 又…又… gives two qualities of the same apples. 甜 (tián) describes the taste.

exercises.prompt: Say: “My Chinese is getting better and better.”
exercises.explanation: 越来越 before 好 shows that the speaker’s Chinese keeps improving over time.
不要 asks that something be left out. 加糖 means to add sugar, and 不 is pronounced bú before fourth-tone 要.

exercises.prompt: Say: “I did not understand what I heard.”
exercises.english: I did not understand what I heard.
exercises.explanation: 懂 is the result of 听. 没听懂 means that listening did not lead to understanding.

exercises.prompt: Say: “I know this teacher.” Use familiarity, not knowing a fact.
exercises.explanation: 认识 expresses familiarity with a person. 位 is a polite classifier for people.

exercises.pinyin: Zhè shǒu Zhōngwén gē hěn hǎotīng.
exercises.explanation: 首 is the classifier for songs. 好听 describes something pleasant to hear.

exercises.prompt: Say: “I want to buy this coat.” Include its classifier.
exercises.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi zhè jiàn wàitào.
exercises.english: I want to buy this coat.
exercises.explanation: 想 comes before the action 买. 件 is the clothing classifier and goes between 这 and 外套.
一起 means together. The final particle 吧 turns the sentence into a suggestion.

exercises.pinyin: Wǒ zài yì jiā gōngsī gōngzuò.
exercises.explanation: The location phrase 在一家公司 comes before 工作. 家 is the classifier for companies.
工资 means salary or wages. Put 不 directly before 高 to say the salary is low or modest.

exercises.prompt: Say: “I want to drink water.” Do not confuse water and tax.
exercises.explanation: In 喝水, 水 (shuǐ) is third-tone water. 税 (shuì) is fourth-tone tax.
明天 sets the time. 再 before 来 signals that the visit will happen again.

exercises.prompt: Say: “This one is cheaper than that one.”
exercises.english: This one is cheaper than that one.
exercises.explanation: Use A 比 B + adjective. The item described comes before 比 and the comparison item comes after it.

review.title: Qualities, sounds and similar words
review.text: 甜 (tián) means sweet and 糖 (táng) means sugar. 好吃 (hǎochī) describes pleasing taste and 好听 (hǎotīng) describes pleasing sound. 公司 (gōngsī) means company and 工资 (gōngzī) means wages. Review each Hanzi form together with its pinyin.

review.title: Similar constructions, different jobs
review.text: 又…又… (yòu…yòu…) joins two descriptions. 越来越 (yuèláiyuè) shows an increasing change. 有点 (yǒudiǎn) before an adjective expresses a mild quality or complaint. 一点 (yìdiǎn) after an adjective asks for or describes a small difference.

review.title: Descriptions before a noun
review.text: In the imported-apples example, the phrase describing where the apples come from goes before 的苹果 (de píngguǒ). When you see 是 (shì) and 的 (de) together, look at what 的 attaches to and check whether the sentence describes a noun or highlights a detail about a past event.

review.title: Tone changes and neutral syllables
review.text: Say yì jīn, yìdiǎn and yì shǒu before the non-fourth tones in these examples, and yí jiàn and yígòng before fourth tones. Compare bú yào with bù xíng. Neutral syllables have no accent marks. Pinyin shows dictionary tones for strings of third tones, and their actual pronunciation depends on how the words are grouped.

review.title: A different yī
review.text: In 洗衣机 (xǐyījī), 衣 (yī) means clothes and keeps its first tone. The tone-change rules for 一 (yī), the number one, apply to that character. In 空调 (kōngtiáo), air conditioning, 调 is pronounced tiáo.

review.title: Your reading recording
review.text: Record yourself reading the exact “My Diary” text from your teacher. Use the lesson’s rehearsal checklist to prepare. Read slowly enough to keep word groups intact. Replay the recording and identify two or three specific places to improve.
